title: Babylon Is Jerusalem (Parts 1 and 2)
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Argues that the harlot Babylon of Revelation 17-18 is first-century Jerusalem, from the 'great city' of 11:8, the priestly colours, the blood of the prophets and the contrast with the New Jerusalem.

title: Revelation: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary (Anchor Yale Bible 38A)
author: Craig R. Koester
summary: Major critical commentary stressing Revelation's engagement with the social, religious and economic world of Roman Asia; reads Babylon as Rome and its pattern.
note: URL is a Themelios review confirming the publication details.

title: The Rise of Babylon: Sign of the End Times
author: Charles H. Dyer (with Angela Elwell Hunt)
summary: Dispensational argument that the Old Testament prophecies against Babylon were never literally fulfilled, so a literal Babylon on the Euphrates must be rebuilt and judged in the end time.
note: URL is a 1991 Christianity Today report on the book, not the book itself.

title: Babylon in Bible Prophecy
author: Andy Woods
summary: Pre-Trib Research Center article arguing that Babylon in Revelation 17-18 is a literal future city rebuilt on the Euphrates in Iraq, against symbolic readings.

title: The Climax of Prophecy: Studies on the Book of Revelation
author: Richard Bauckham
summary: Collected studies including 'The Economic Critique of Rome in Revelation 18' and a long treatment of Nero, the Nero redivivus legend and 666.

title: The Days of Vengeance: An Exposition of the Book of Revelation
author: David Chilton

title: Revelation (Baker Exegetical Commentary on the New Testament)
author: Grant R. Osborne
